channels.name: Blender Studio
channels.description: Open movies and animation experiments from the Blender Foundation. Free to watch, free to share, made with open-source tools.

channels.name: NASA
channels.description: Exploring the universe and our home planet. Public-domain footage from the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

channels.name: Nomad Lens
channels.description: Slow travel, city lights and quiet corners of the planet. Short visual diaries, no narration.

channels.name: Kitchen Theory
channels.description: Simple food, shot slowly. No twenty-minute intros, no life story, just dinner.

channels.name: Neon Sessions
channels.description: Live sets and loud rooms. Turn it up and pretend you're in the front row.

channels.name: Devlog
channels.description: Building things late at night and talking about it. Code, coffee, questionable decisions.

videos.title: Big Buck Bunny
videos.description:
A giant rabbit with a big heart teaches three bullying rodents a lesson in the forest. The Blender Foundation's classic open movie, made entirely with free and open-source software.

Licensed CC-BY. Watch, remix, share.

videos.title: Earth Views from the International Space Station
videos.description:
Sit back and watch our planet roll by from low Earth orbit. A quiet compilation of Earth views captured by crews aboard the International Space Station — coastlines, clouds, city lights and the thin blue line of the atmosphere.

Footage: NASA. Public domain.

videos.title: Sintel
videos.description:
A lone warrior searches for her lost dragon companion across a snowbound world. Blender's third open movie, and still one of the most beautiful things the community has made.

Licensed CC-BY. Directed by Colin Levy.

videos.title: Artemis I Launches to the Moon (Official NASA Recap)
videos.description:
The Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft lift off from Kennedy Space Center, beginning a 1.4-million-mile journey around the Moon. A recap of the Artemis I mission, the first integrated flight test of the hardware that will carry humans back to the lunar surface.

Footage: NASA. Public domain.

videos.title: City lights after midnight
videos.description: No narration. Just a city breathing after midnight.

videos.title: Tears of Steel
videos.description:
Amsterdam, 2057. A team of scientists tries to undo a robot uprising by repairing a broken memory. Blender's live-action and VFX open movie, shot on real streets and finished with open-source tools.

Licensed CC-BY. Directed by Ian Hubert.

videos.title: James Webb Space Telescope: An Overview
videos.description:
How the James Webb Space Telescope sees the universe in infrared, why its mirror is gold, and what its first images actually tell us. A clear, friendly overview of the most ambitious space observatory ever built.

Footage: NASA. Public domain.

videos.title: One pan, one flame 🔥
videos.description: Dinner and a show, in about fifteen seconds.

videos.title: The Aurora Named STEVE
videos.description:
STEVE — Strong Thermal Emission Velocity Enhancement — is a glowing purple ribbon that appears in the night sky. Citizen scientists helped NASA figure out what it is and why it looks so different from a normal aurora.

Footage: NASA. Public domain.

videos.title: Front row, lights down
videos.description: The moment before the first song. You know the feeling.

videos.title: A city that never stops moving
videos.description: One intersection, eight seconds, a thousand tiny stories.

videos.title: Meanwhile, At the Bottom of the Ocean
videos.description:
A short trip to the seafloor, where NASA satellites help us understand the ocean's role in the climate system. The deep sea is still one of the least explored places on Earth.

Footage: NASA. Public domain.

videos.title: Sunday kitchen, no recipe needed
videos.description: A quiet kitchen, a sharp knife, and nowhere to be.

videos.title: Mars Chopper Ready for a Spin
videos.description:
NASA's Mars Helicopter, Ingenuity, gets ready for its first flight on another world. A small rotorcraft that turned into one of the most remarkable engineering stories of the decade.

Footage: NASA. Public domain.

videos.title: Golden hour over the skyline
videos.description: The ten minutes a city looks like a postcard.

videos.title: Elephants Dream
videos.description:
Two strangers wander a strange mechanical world that keeps rearranging itself around them. The first Blender open movie, released in 2006 and still wonderfully weird.

Licensed CC-BY.

videos.title: Hands up. That's the whole video.
videos.description: You can hear this without sound.

videos.title: How Can I See the Northern Lights? We Asked a NASA Expert
videos.description:
Where, when, and how to catch the aurora borealis — plus why the best viewing is usually nowhere near a city. A NASA expert answers the question everyone asks.

Footage: NASA. Public domain.

videos.title: Kuala Lumpur in 8 seconds
videos.description: The skyline, the haze, the towers. A very short postcard.

videos.title: The ten-second sizzle
videos.description: Butter, garlic, and a pan that's already too hot.

videos.title: NISAR: Tracking Earth's Changes From Space
videos.description:
The NISAR mission will scan nearly all of Earth's land and ice surfaces twice every 12 days, measuring movement as small as a centimeter. A joint NASA and ISRO mission to watch our planet change in near real time.

Footage: NASA. Public domain.

videos.title: The band, the stage, the noise
videos.description: Small venue, big sound. Best way to spend a Friday.

videos.title: Driving into the night
videos.description: Headlights, exit signs, and a destination you don't need.

videos.title: The 2am commit
videos.description: The bug is fixed. The tests pass. Do not touch anything else.

videos.title: Plating, but make it simple
videos.description: The last ten seconds of cooking are the most important ones.

videos.title: Ship it before sunrise
videos.description: A deadline, a dark room, and one more coffee.

videos.title: Where the ocean meets the sky
videos.description: A minute of nothing but waves. On purpose.

videos.title: Terminal green hits different
videos.description: No talking. Just code scrolling on a screen at a reasonable hour.

big-buck-bunny.author: Mika
big-buck-bunny.text: The animation still holds up unbelievably well. That butterfly scene!

big-buck-bunny.author: Jonas
big-buck-bunny.text: Watched this in 2008 on a 480p monitor. It still feels like magic.

big-buck-bunny.author: Priya
big-buck-bunny.text: The fact that it's basically a silent film is such an underrated choice.

sintel.author: Rin
sintel.text: The ending gets me every single time.

sintel.author: Marco
sintel.text: That soundtrack. That final shot. No notes.

sintel.author: Dana
sintel.text: I show this to everyone who says open-source software can't make art.

tears-of-steel.author: Theo
tears-of-steel.text: The VFX breakdown for this is even better than the film.

elephants-dream.author: Sam
elephants-dream.text: Still the strangest thing Blender ever made and I love it.

elephants-dream.author: Iris
elephants-dream.text: The machine world design is so far ahead of its time.

earth-from-space.author: Omar
earth-from-space.text: Put this on a loop on the biggest screen you own.

earth-from-space.author: Lena
earth-from-space.text: Ten seconds in and my shoulders dropped. This is why I love ISS footage.

artemis-launch.author: Ben
artemis-launch.text: The slow-motion liftoff at 1:40 is unreal.

artemis-launch.author: Yuki
artemis-launch.text: I was up at 1am watching this live. Still get chills.

artemis-launch.author: Kwame
artemis-launch.text: The sound design in this recap is genuinely cinematic.

webb-overview.author: Priya
webb-overview.text: Explaining infrared this clearly is a skill.

webb-overview.author: Alex
webb-overview.text: Every new Webb image makes the universe feel bigger and smaller at once.

aurora-steve.author: Rin
aurora-steve.text: I saw STEVE once from a plane and had no idea what it was. Thank you for this.

aurora-steve.author: Theo
aurora-steve.text: Citizen science absolutely carrying space weather research.

bottom-of-the-ocean.author: Dana
bottom-of-the-ocean.text: The ocean is genuinely scarier than space.

bottom-of-the-ocean.author: Marco
bottom-of-the-ocean.text: That footage of the seafloor is so calming.

mars-chopper.author: Noor
mars-chopper.text: Flying a helicopter on another planet. Casually.

mars-chopper.author: Sam
mars-chopper.text: It was supposed to be a tech demo and it kept going for years. Wild.

northern-lights.author: Iris
northern-lights.text: Step 1: get away from city lights. Step 2: be lucky.

northern-lights.author: Omar
northern-lights.text: Watched the aurora from Tromsø last winter. Absolutely worth the cold.

northern-lights.author: Lena
northern-lights.text: The explanation of the solar wind is the clearest I've heard.

nisar.author: Kwame
nisar.text: Measuring centimeter-scale movement from orbit never stops being impressive.

nisar.author: Ben
nisar.text: This is the kind of mission that quietly changes everything.
